findings.title: No solver-level check of the exporter on any layout other than Case 4; FastHenry and l2_layout differ by 24% on a generated layout at the thin level
findings.detail: The tests are structural: areas, counts, equivalence classes, read order, and a line-for-line match with the P4 research exporter, which comes from the same code. The only FastHenry-vs-l2_layout agreement on record is P4's, on Case 4. I solved the generated layout (seed 7, 2 dies per switch, lattice origin at -8 mm) both ways. FastHenry at cell 0.5 mm, plane 2 mm, one thickness filament (nh=1) gave L = 13.932 nH at 10 MHz; l2_layout at refinement 0 gave 11.220 nH, a gap of +24%. The same comparison on Case 4 is about +8% at nh=1 and about +3% at P4's k1 level (23.65 vs about 22.96 nH). The likely cause is the thickness model, not the deck. This stack has only 0.38 mm between the trace bottom and the backside-Cu top, against 0.835 mm in Case 4. At nh=1 the currents sit at mid-thickness, which stretches that gap to 0.68 mm (1.8x); in Case 4 the stretch is 1.24x. A confirming FastHenry run at the k1 knobs (nh=3) hit its 90-minute background limit and was stopped before writing Zc.mat. A generalisation error, for example in wire-foot contacts on corner-tied cells (all 14 contacts tie four cells at 0.5 mm here), is therefore not excluded at the solver level.
findings.evidence: $TMPDIR/fh/gen0_c0.5/Zc.mat: 1e7 -> 0.00306988 +0.875386j (13.932 nH); 2e7 -> 1.75076j (13.932 nH). l2_layout.loop_inductance(gen0, [1e7, 2e7], refinement=0): L_H = [1.12204e-08, 1.11150e-08], solver_tol_rel_L_max 1.8e-5. facts: n_shorted_segments = 56 = 14 contacts x 4. $TMPDIR/fh/gen0_k1: run killed at its time limit, no result.
findings.suggested_check: Solve the generated layout at the k1 knobs (cell 0.5, plane 2, nh 3, wire_sub 2) with a timeout of about 3 h and confirm the gap drops to Case 4's few percent before E004 relies on non-Case-4 decks.

findings.title: FHLevel() defaults to nh_trace = nh_plane = 1, which is strongly biased on thin-ceramic stacks
findings.detail: With one filament through the thickness, trace and plane currents sit at mid-thickness. On the generated stack (0.3 mm trace, 0.3 mm backside Cu, 0.38 mm gap) this inflates L far more than on Case 4, where nh 1 -> 3 changed L by 4.5%. The module says it freezes no level, so this is a usage hazard, not a defect.
findings.evidence: Generated-stack z from to_conductors(): backside_cu 3.1-3.4 mm, top Cu 3.78-4.08 mm. Case 4: backside_cu 1.001-1.201 mm, top Cu 2.036-2.236 mm.
findings.suggested_check: Document in the module that nh=1 is a smoke-test level only.

findings.title: facts['n_filaments'] and direct_mem_est_gb are pre-refinement counts; FastHenry adds filaments to distributed-die decks
findings.detail: On the Case 4 distributed deck, FastHenry reported 8816 filaments before its 'multipole refine' and 8912 after: it split filaments of the 96 short, wide die columns. The deck facts report 8816, so the memory estimate is slightly low. The short and tab decks matched FastHenry's counts exactly.
findings.evidence: distributed_point/log.txt: 'Total number of filaments before multipole refine: 8816', 'after multipole refine: 8912'. short_point 8416/8344, short_point_p2 14436/14364 and short_tab 14454/14382 (filaments/segments) match the facts exactly.
findings.suggested_check: Note in the facts that counts are before FastHenry's own refinement.

findings.title: The equal-GMD square wire changes cross-section area and perimeter
findings.detail: a = 0.87104 d is correct for equal GMD (0.7788 r / 0.44705; Grover). Its area is 0.759 d^2 against 0.785 d^2 for the disc (DC resistance +3.5%), and its perimeter is 3.48 d against 3.14 d (lower skin-effect R). The equivalent HF radius, 0.59 a = 0.514 d against 0.5 d, keeps L within about 3% in the log term. This only matters if R is compared.

findings.title: Tab posts are vertical and cannot couple to gplane eddy currents
findings.detail: In PEEC, perpendicular filaments have zero partial mutual inductance, so the posts' interaction with the horizontal planes is not modelled. The measured tab-minus-point change of +0.085 nH (both at plane 2 mm) is consistent with my hand estimate: each 3x3-filament post (9 columns of 1 x 1 mm, 2.1 mm long) adds about 0.30 nH of partial self-inductance, about +0.6 nH for both, offset by less spreading inductance at the wider injection footprint.
findings.evidence: short_point_p2 25.5659 nH; short_tab 25.6513 nH at 10 MHz.

independent_checks_performed: Ran the definition-of-done commands: uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_fasthenry.py gave 55 passed; ruff check on both files passed.

Ran the provisioned FastHenry 3.0wr (direct solver) on Case 4 decks for all variants. short/point (1/4 mm) exit 0, L = 25.796 nH at both frequencies. P4's multipole value for the identical deck is 25.787 nH (-3.3e-4, the same as P4's own direct-vs-multipole figure). distributed/point 27.192 nH (+5.4%). short/point at plane 2 mm 25.566 nH. short/tab at plane 2 mm 25.651 nH. Every Zc.mat holds exactly the 1e+07 and 2e+07 entries, and parse_zc parses them.

Compared the exporter's filament and segment facts with FastHenry's own counts: they match exactly for the short and tab decks, and gplane seg1/seg2 segment bookkeeping is confirmed. The distributed deck is refined by FastHenry from 8816 to 8912 filaments.
Hand estimate of the tab post inductance from rectangular-bar partial self and mutual formulas: about 0.30 nH per post. The sign and size of the measured tab-minus-point change are plausible.
Re-derived the equal-GMD square side: 0.7788 / (2 x 0.44705) = 0.87104 d.
Exported 8 generated layouts (2, 4 and 6 dies per switch, seeds 7, 11 and 3) at 0.5 mm: all export. At 1 mm all are refused as off-lattice, which is l2_layout's behaviour.

Generated layout (seed 7, non-zero origin): the FastHenry multipole solve at 0.5/2 mm, nh=1 gave 13.932 nH; l2_layout at refinement 0 gave 11.220 nH (10 MHz). The k1-level FastHenry run meant to separate thickness error from an exporter error was stopped at its 90-minute background time limit with no result.
Read l2_layout's end_contact, contact_at, _nearest_cell and die-short code and confirmed that the exporter's die-group, wire-end and nearest-cell rules match it.
caveats: Verified scope: the decks are readable by FastHenry and solve for all four F6 variant combinations on Case 4 at cell 1 mm, and for the default model on one generated layout at 0.5 mm. The values are plausible, and the default deck reproduces P4's Case 4 result.

Not verified: agreement between FastHenry and l2_layout on any non-Case-4 layout at a converged thickness level. At nh=1 the gap is +24% on a generated layout, against about +8% for Case 4 at the same level. I attribute this to the thin-ceramic stack, but the nh=3 confirmation run was stopped at its 90-minute background time limit with no result. Re-running it needs a timeout of about 3 hours.

The tab and distributed variants were checked only for syntax and solvability and against a hand-estimate sanity check. Their physical validity as diagnostics rests on the documented modelling assumptions: metal die block, single-filament columns, no post-to-plane coupling.

The test suite is structural and proves nothing about impedance. Its FastHenry-reader emulator (read_errors) stands in for the real binary, and the faithful-port test compares against code of the same lineage.
